transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-12
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Clara Ng (CEO), Devon Lee (CTO), Miguel Torres (Head of Eng), Anika Patel (VP Product), Liam O'Connor (Head of Sales), Rachel Kim (Head of People) + company-wide dial-in

Summary: Quick product & infra updates, Dedicated and Private progress, Q3 priorities, hiring update, then open Q&A. Some auto-gen notes: timestamps and speaker labels approximate; occasional mis-transcriptions (e.g., KV cash / KV cache; Redood Dedicated).

[00:00] Clara: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Um, I know it's a busy week so we'll keep this to about an hour. Quick agenda: product, infra, hires, and Q&A. Devon's got a performance update and Miguel will walk through Dedicated numbers. Anika will cover roadmap. Rachel, quick hiring update.

[00:30] Devon: Cool, thanks Clara. So from an infra perspective, latency has been holding steady. P50 on the hosted API is down to 45ms for our short-seq gen profiles, p95 about 220ms, which is an improvement after the kernel selection changes. There is still some tail at high concurrency when we run multi-tenant batching; we're rolling out a patch to the batching scheduler this week.

[01:10] Miguel: Yeah, and on Dedicated, we finished our Q2 throughput benchmarks. The dedicated pools with the new quantized runtime hit about 1.9x throughput vs last quarter on the mid-length sequence workload. Note: these are lab numbers - customers under prod load see slightly different numbers, but the gap holds. I'll share the spreadsheet after the call.

[01:50] Anika: A couple of product highlights: streaming improvements, better function-calling ergonomics, and a small pilot of structured outputs with a couple of customers. We're also rolling out an early preview of the Redwood Optimize suggestions UI - it's basically prescriptive batching and quant recommendations per route.

[02:30] Liam: On GTM, we've updated the pricing tiers for Dedicated and added a burst option for Reserved pools. Early feedback from two pilot accounts has been positive; the main asks are around clearer SLAs and more transparent unit economics per-model.

[03:00] Rachel: Hiring - we're on track to close three senior IC roles this quarter, and we're opening two more for infra (senior infra SWE) and one staff PM. People is also running manager training next week.

[03:30] Clara: Thanks. Quick reminder on Private rollout - the VPC/on-prem timelines slipped a couple weeks because of an integration issue with a customer's KMS provider. Anika, can you say more?

[04:00] Anika: Yeah, we hit a snag with the HSM/KMS integration where key wrapping behavior differed across providers. That caused audit log mismatches for one customer. We're working with the partner to standardize the flow; plan is to have the fix staged by end of the week and pushed to canary early next week. We're also expanding the Private docs set - SAML/SSO, RBAC examples, and a SOC 2 section.

[04:40] Miguel: On the technical side, we also observed an edge case in model-variant fallback - when the primary model runs out of mem we fallback to a quantized variant, but there's a short spike in latency while the KV cash warms up - sorry, KV cache warms up. We'll add a pre-warm step to avoid that spike.

[05:10] Devon: Just to add, kernel selection improvements reduced some of the overhead, but to avoid the spike we may route warmups to a low-cost buffer pool. That ties into cost optimization work.

[05:40] Clara: Great. Q3 goals - short version: 1) make Dedicated latency predictable under commit workloads, 2) finish Private GA for VPC deployments, 3) reduce per-token cost for common PLG flows by 20% through Optimize and better batching, 4) hire for infra senior roles. We'll distribute a detailed goals doc after this.

[06:15] Anika: On roadmap cadence - we're shifting to monthly quality gates tied to real prompt sets (the eval harness). That means every month we run a small regression suite capturing latency, cost, and quality on canonical prompt sets and send alerts on regressions.

[06:50] Liam: Sales ops note: revise renewal language to call out fallback policies and failure modes. Customers want clarity: if Dedicated capacity is constrained, what's the fallback? We now support model variants and cross-region routing; we need to standardize messaging.

[07:20] Miguel: We'll draft a short doc on routing policies for the sales kit - can include examples: route by latency SLO, cost cap, region priority, and automatic fallbacks to compatible variants.

[07:50] Audience question (Slack poll): Is there a plan to support on-prem air-gapped installs?

[08:00] Devon: Short answer: yes. We have an air-gapped packaging plan; it's targeted for the Private on-prem release. The main blockers are packaging the runtime and the control plane connectors in a way that meets common E2E compliance checks.

[08:30] Clara: Ok we have a couple of live questions - I'll try to get through as many as possible.

[08:45] Question from Eng: Will we deprecate any legacy instrumentation?

[08:50] Miguel: We'll deprecate the old detailed request-metrics collector in favor of the new lightweight tracer that can be turned on for a route. We'll announce deprecation waves and provide migration scripts.

[09:20] Question from Sales: Any push for volume discounts?

[09:25] Liam: Yes, we're formalizing a volume discount framework for high-commit Dedicated deals. Sales + Finance will publish the framework next week.

[10:00] Clara: Quick note on NPS and support - CS has been doing a great job lowering response times. We need to keep pushing on escalations for early Dedicated customers; those are high-touch.

[10:20] Rachel: Also an FYI on people ops - internal mobility is encouraged. We had two successful role shifts last month. And we'll host a town hall for managers on 2026-06-18.

[11:00] Audience question: How are we prioritizing research vs product for inference optimizations?

[11:10] Devon: We balance immediate runway items (kernel opt, batching) with longer-term compilers work. Research owns a runway backlog and triages into product epics.

[11:40] Miguel: Also translation to customers: when we recommend quantization we add expected quality delta and cost savings in the Optimize UI so customers can make an informed choice.

[12:10] Live Q&A continues - sample exchange: attendee: "Will Dedicated support multi-tenant pools within a single customer?" Miguel: "Yes, with RBAC and quotas; we'll have docs out."

[12:40] Clara: Ok team - closing comments. Please remember to review the Q3 goals doc when it lands, and prioritize any tasks that unblock Private GA. Any final quick notes?

[13:00] Anika: One more - we're improving the eval harness onboarding so product PMs can add prompt sets without Eng help, should cut cycle time.

[13:20] Liam: I'll be running a customer feedback review next Tuesday; please add any pilot feedback to the spreadsheet I'm sharing in #sales.

[13:40] Rachel: Reminder: we have a company offsite planning workshop next month; RSVP by end of week.

[14:00] Clara: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with slides and recording. Meeting adjourned.
